messages:
Maya (AE): Heads up — MedicaOne signed off on a 2-node private POC next Tue. They want a minimal validate: 2 GPU worker nodes, 1 control plane. They also want an automatic fallback to our hosted API if the private route fails. Need a concise preflight checklist we can send their infra/security teams.
Leo (Solutions Eng): Nice. I'll own the technical checklist. Quick clarifying Q: do they want us to push the operator or will they pull from their registry?
Maya (AE): They prefer us to provide images but will try pulling first. If not, airgapped delivery OK.
Devon (Field Eng): For hardware/drivers: recommend Linux distro with kernel >= 5.15, NVIDIA driver >= 525.60, CUDA toolkit >= 12.1. If they have A100/H100-class cards, confirm driver/CUDA combos match. Ask them to report `nvidia-smi -L` output.
Priya (Security): From Sec: we cannot accept long-lived kubeconfigs. If they give a kubeconfig for bootstrap it must be time-limited (24h) and source-IP allowlisted. Alternatively they should create a namespaced service account and provide token + RBAC YAML. No cluster-admin. Also need their cert/key management notes (rotation cadence, storage location: KMS/HSM?).
Chris (SRE): Network rules: allow outbound to registry.redwood.ai:443, allow DNS (udp/53), NTP (udp/123), and outbound to our fallback API hostnames on 443. If their infra is fully airgapped we will provide signed image tarballs + manifest and an installer bundle.
Leo (Solutions Eng): I'll prepare two artifacts: 1) minimal RBAC YAML they can apply if they prefer creating the SA; 2) a bootstrap playbook for us to run with a short-lived kubeconfig.
Maya (AE): Also capture pricing notes: short Dedicated pool estimate in the one-pager and fallback hosted usage cost (metered).
Devon (Field Eng): Add validation commands we want them to run and paste outputs. Put these in a code block so they can copy/paste:
```
# on each worker node
nvidia-smi -L
nvidia-smi -q | head -n 60
uname -r
cat /etc/os-release
# from control plane
kubectl get nodes -o wide
kubectl version --short
# container runtime checks
crictl images | head -n 20
# kernel messages (watch for driver OOMs)
dmesg | tail -n 200
```
Priya (Security): Also ask for their private DNS/prefix details (split-horizon) since operator may need to resolve internal registry names. And confirm whether image pulls must go via an internal proxy.
Chris (SRE): For quick stress check (optional) tell them to run a lightweight multi-worker container we provide and watch `dmesg` for GPU allocation failures. We'll give the exact command in the playbook.
Leo (Solutions Eng): Minimal RBAC snippet (they can apply if they create SA):
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: redwood-operator-sa
  namespace: redwood-system
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: redwood-operator-role
  namespace: redwood-system
rules:
  - apiGroups: [""]
    resources: ["pods","secrets","configmaps"]
    verbs: ["get","list","watch","create","update","patch","delete"]
---
# Bind role to SA
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: redwood-operator-binding
  namespace: redwood-system
subjects:
  - kind: ServiceAccount
    name: redwood-operator-sa
    namespace: redwood-system
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: redwood-operator-role
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```
Maya (AE): If they prefer we bring a kubeconfig, remind them to set expiration and IP allowlist.
Priya (Security): Also need a short statement from them about who owns the node credentials and where private keys are stored. If they use an external KMS/HSM list the provider and key id.
Devon (Field Eng): Kubernetes versions: we support 1.26-1.28. Ask them to avoid older minor releases. If they run 1.25 or older we can discuss mitigations but won't guarantee runtime behaviour.
Chris (SRE): Logging and observability: they should forward node-level syslogs (or allow us to ship a sidecar that reads driver logs). For telco/enterprise networks confirm MTU > 1400 for large payloads.
Leo (Solutions Eng): I'll prepare the one-pager with the checklist, the code snippets above, the RBAC YAML, and the fallback API key plan. I'll also include a short step-by-step for airgap image import.
infra-bot: apiKey:create requested by Leo (Solutions Eng) -> created scoped key: medicaone-poc-fallback (read: inference-only) expires=14d
Maya (AE): Great — I'll send this out to the buyer and schedule a 60m kickoff with infra + security + ops. Who wants to join?
Chris (SRE): I can join first 30m for network/egress and image questions.
Devon (Field Eng): I'll join for the latter 30m to validate drivers and run the stress check.
Priya (Security): I'll attend to walk through RBAC and KMS requirements.
Leo (Solutions Eng): I'll run the demo operator steps and hand off to Devon for debugging.
Maya (AE): Thanks team. I'll ping back with buyer responses and their `nvidia-smi`/k8s outputs. Please watch for the thread and the kickoff invite. :white_check_mark:
